classification.difficultyReason: Locate two quartile positions, estimate their heights from a cumulative frequency polygon and subtract.

content.prompt: The heights of 400 students were measured. The results are displayed in this cumulative frequency polygon. Use the polygon to estimate the interquartile range.

spec.description: Unshaded cumulative frequency polygon with a dense rectangular grid, height labels from 100 to 200 cm in steps of 10 and cumulative frequency labels from 0 to 400 in steps of 50.

mathematics.vertexPrecision: Intermediate vertices are readings from the printed graph, not separately supplied numerical data.

spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied axes, grid and polygon are visible; quartile readings and calculations belong to the answer.

answer.worked:
There are $400$ students. The quartile positions are
$$\begin{aligned}
\text{Lower quartile position} &= \frac{400}{4} \\
&= 100 \\
\text{Upper quartile position} &= \frac{3}{4}\times400 \\
&= 300.
\end{aligned}$$
Read horizontally from cumulative frequencies $100$ and $300$ to the polygon, then vertically to the height axis:
$$Q_1\approx136\text{ cm},\qquad Q_3\approx172\text{ cm}.$$
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{IQR} &= Q_3-Q_1 \\
&\approx172-136 \\
&=36\text{ cm}.
\end{aligned}$$
